chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from his father from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said:

Whoever fasts the first day of Rajab in desire for Allah's reward -- Mighty and Majestic is He -- Paradise is made mandatory for him. Whoever fasts a day in its middle will be able to intercede for the like of Rabi'a and Mudar. Whoever fasts a day at its end, Allah -- Mighty and Majestic is He -- will make him from the kings of Paradise and he will intercede for his father, his mother, his son, his daughter, his brother, his sister, his paternal uncle, his paternal aunt, his maternal uncle, his maternal aunt, his acquaintances, and his neighbours, even if among them was one deserving of the Fire.

key_terms.رَبِيعَةَ وَمُضَرَ: Rabi'a and Mudar: two large Arab tribal confederations, used to express an enormous number of people
key_terms.مُلُوكِ الْجَنَّةِ: Kings of Paradise: the highest station of honor in the afterlife

ai.seo_question: What are the three rewards for fasting in Rajab according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) described the graduated rewards for fasting in Rajab: fasting the first day guarantees Paradise; fasting a middle day grants intercession for as many people as the tribes of Rabi'a and Mudar; fasting the last day elevates one to kingship in Paradise with intercession for all relatives and acquaintances, even if they deserved Hellfire. This hadith was transmitted through Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from his father from Imam al-Rida.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (rh) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Kufi narrated to us from `Ali b. al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Faddal from his father from Abu’l Hasan `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as). He said:

Whoever fasts the first day of Rajab in hope for Allah’s reward, Paradise will be made mandatory for him. Whoever fasts a day in the middle [of Rajab] will be able to intercede for the like of Rabi` and Mudar. Whoever fasts a day at the end [of Rajab], Allah will make him from the kings of Paradise; and he will intercede for his father, his mother, his son, his daughter, his brother, his sister, his paternal uncle, his paternal aunt, his maternal uncle, his maternal aunt, his acquaintances, and his neighbours, even if Hell was made mandatory for some of them.
